# Security Checklist: GitHub Pilot Issue Ingest and Eligibility

**Purpose**: Validate that SPEC-009C1 requirements and plan artifacts define credential-safe, operator-controlled GitHub pilot ingest behavior without live-secret dependencies, hidden synthetic mutations, or private terminal context in smoke evidence.
**Created**: 2026-05-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Do automated test requirements fully prohibit live GitHub credentials, live GitHub fetch/create/edit/close paths, and live-mutation smoke-script mode in CI? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, Plan §Constraints, Quickstart §Automated Fixture Coverage]
- [ ] CHK002 Do operator-script requirements fully prohibit echoing or persisting raw tokens, Authorization headers, API keys, GitHub credentials, credential-like values, and matched secret substrings? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020, Spec §FR-023, Data Model §Pilot Smoke Evidence]
- [ ] CHK003 Do synthetic fallback requirements fully require reuse-before-create, explicit live-mutation opt-in, and no auto-close or auto-delete behavior? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, Data Model §Synthetic Fallback Issue, Contract §Synthetic Fallback Contract]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the manual smoke checklist requirement include candidate selection, synthetic fallback, duplicate prevention, local-only exclusion, side-effect checks, cleanup instructions, and cleanup-safe evidence capture? [Resolved: Spec §FR-018, Spec §FR-023, Quickstart §Manual Live Smoke Path]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the boundary between credential-free automated tests and credential-required manual smoke actions clear enough to prevent CI from depending on `GITHUB_TOKEN` or operator secrets? [Clarity, Spec §Clarifications Session 1, Spec §FR-012, Quickstart §Automated Fixture Coverage]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "explicit live-mutation opt-in" specific enough to prevent synthetic issue creation from being hidden in normal app runtime, default sync, automatic polling, or fixture tests? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, Spec §FR-013, Research §Synthetic Fallback]
- [ ] CHK007 Are allowed smoke evidence fields stated clearly enough that reviewers can inspect results without raw terminal scrollback, environment dumps, or private secret context? [Resolved: Spec §FR-023, Data Model §Pilot Smoke Evidence, Contract §Existing Operator Sync Contract]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Do test, quickstart, and contract artifacts consistently require mocked or fixture GitHub clients for automated candidate selection, synthetic fallback, and operator-triggered sync coverage? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, Plan §Testing, Contract §Synthetic Fallback Contract]
- [ ] CHK009 Do operator-script redaction rules align with the constitution's rule that boundary errors provide actionable context without leaking raw secret or untrusted payload material? [Consistency, Constitution §XIII, Spec §FR-020, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK010 Do synthetic fallback requirements align across spec, data model, contract, and quickstart so creation is always visible, operator-controlled, and absent from normal runtime sync? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, Data Model §Synthetic Fallback Issue, Contract §Synthetic Fallback Contract, Quickstart §Manual Live Smoke Path]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK011 Can automated verification objectively prove that tests do not require `GITHUB_TOKEN` and do not call live GitHub mutation paths? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §SC-007, Quickstart §Fixture Expectations]
- [ ] CHK012 Can operator-script failure evidence be objectively reviewed while showing only operation names, candidate identifiers, stable error codes, counts, booleans, or hashes? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-020, Spec §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK013 Can synthetic fallback creation be objectively distinguished from normal runtime sync by evidence of explicit live-mutation opt-in and reuse-before-create behavior? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §FR-011, Spec §SC-001, Contract §Synthetic Fallback Contract]

## Scenario And Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK014 Are security-relevant failure cases covered for missing credentials, insufficient permissions, GitHub API failure, malformed or partial payloads, fallback label mismatch, and operator sync failure? [Coverage, Spec §SC-007, Quickstart §Fixture Expectations]
- [ ] CHK015 Are smoke-evidence leakage cases covered for terminal scrollback, environment dumps, token values, Authorization headers, API keys, GitHub credentials, raw credential material, credential-like values, and matched secret substrings? [Resolved: Spec §FR-023, Data Model §Pilot Smoke Evidence]
- [ ] CHK016 Are side-effect absence checks required for failed or denied credential paths so security failures cannot create local-only pilot tasks, dispatch attempts, successors, runs, artifacts, or remediation activities? [Coverage, Spec §FR-015, Spec §FR-020, Spec §FR-022]

## Dependencies And Assumptions

- [ ] CHK017 Are manual live smoke dependencies documented for GitHub availability, sufficient operator credentials, required repo labels, and operator access to trigger the existing sync seam? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK018 Are external credential-handling assumptions constrained to operator-provided credentials without requiring new credential storage, token persistence, or production evidence surfaces in SPEC-009C1? [Assumption, Spec §FR-012, Spec §FR-016, Plan §Structure Decision]
